newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Italian Serie A games scheduled for Sunday (league positions in parentheses, all kick-off times 1400 GMT):

Bologna still have hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Cup while Cagliari desperately need an away point to help their relegation battle. Davide Fontolan and Swede Kennet Andersson lead the Bologna attack while Uruguayan Dario Silva may replace the suspended Roberto Muzzi in the Cagliari attack alongside Sandro Tovalieri.

Udinese may fancy their chances in this UEFA place battle. Fiorentina are without Portuguese midfielder Rui Costa and Swedish midfielder Stefan Schwarz, both out for the rest of the season through injury, while Brazilian striker Oliveira and defender Daniele Carnasciali are both suspended. Udinese may field an impressive trio of German Oliver Bierhoff, Brazilian Amoroso and Paolo Poggi in attack.

Relegation-threatened Perugia may prove more motivated than Lazio, who look well positioned to win a UEFA Cup place. Lazio coach Dino Zoff may drop Igor Protti, scorer of a late equaliser in last week's 1-1 derby draw with Roma, leaving Pierluigi Casiraghi and Giuseppe Signori in attack. Perugia look to Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri in attack

Even this season's disappointing Milan ought to be able to see off bottom-of-table Reggiana, a side whose relegation is all but mathematically certain. Liberian George Weah and Roberto Baggio lead the Milan attack, Russian Igor Simutenkov will cut a lone figure up front for Reggiana.

Napoli won their first game for 102 days when they defeated Vicenza 1-0 in the Italian Cup final first leg in Naples on Thursday and that win may spur them on against Roma. In truth, Napoli are too close to the relegation zone for comfort. Napoli's Brazilian playmaker Andre Cruz is suspended while Alfredo Aglietti and Nicola Caccia are likely to resume their attacking partnership. Roma look to a three-man attack of Francesco Totti, Marco Delvecchio and Argentine Abel Balbo.

Parma have to win to keep up the pressure on leaders Juventus, who lead them by four points. Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo lead the Parma attack but Croatian midfielder Mario Stanic is still out through injury. Vicenza are without their suspended captain Giovanni Lopez and may be feeling the effect of a 1-0 defeat by Napoli in the first leg of the Italian Cup final on Thursday.

Another clash between a relegation threatened side and one still in the UEFA place battle. Atalanta, with leading goalscorer Filippo Inzaghi but without suspended Yugoslav defender Zoran Mirkovic, are unlikely to concede much to a Piacenza side led by Pasquale Luiso and Gian Pietro Piovani.

With howls of protest still ringing in their ears following a disappointing performance in the first leg of the UEFA Cup final, where they lost 1-0 to German side Schalke on Wednesday, Inter cannot afford another slip-up. Frenchmen Jocelyn Angloma and Youri Djorkaeff and English midfielder Paul Ince, who were all suspended for the Schalke game, return, while defender Massimo Paganin is out through suspension. Sampdoria are at full strength, led by captain Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella in attack, with Frenchman Christian Karembeu and Argentine Juan Veron in midfield.

Victory should be relatively straightforward for leaders Juventus against Verona, another side already relegated in all but mathematical certainty. Christian Vieri and Croatia's Alen Boksic lead the Juventus attack, with Alessandro Del Piero on the bench, at least initially. Nicola Zanini and Filippo Maniero
